thread:
maria: triage note: reproduced a read-after-write flake during prefix handoff when eviction and a concurrent write overlap. attaching tiny log snippet.
infra-bot: alert: kvcache-error-rate spike on pool-gamma/node-7
ben: repro steps?
maria: harness: heavy append -> demote -> immediate read loop. ~40-60% locally. sometimes reader sees previous version id.
maria: log:
```
WARN kvcache: stale read prefix=0x12a expected=42 got=41 origin=node-7
```
alex: likely sequence: ownership token moved but commit didn't land before eviction/tombstone cleanup. reader on new owner sees older state.
leo: options: pin demote until commit ack; two-phase handoff; or emit a short-lived grace marker so readers consult previous owner for a small window.
sara: pins can leak memory if writers stall. two-phase adds complexity. grace marker is lightweight but needs TTL tuning.
ben: grace idea sketch: emit grace(prefix, ttl=200ms) on demote; read path checks grace -> forward to prev owner.
jing: forwarding adds tail RPC latency and complexity.
alex: alternative: write a tiny commit-checksum into per-prefix metadata. reads validate checksum; on mismatch retry or forward. fast common case, fallback handles races.
maria: quick local perf: metadata-validate +0.5ms; proxy-forward +1.7ms. CAS retries spike at high qps in microbench.
ben: pragmatic: implement metadata fast-path, and on validation-fail fallback to grace+forward. cheap common case, correctness via fallback.
jing: need telemetry: validation_fail_count, forward_count, avg_forward_latency, grace_expirations, cas_retry_rate.
leo: ops: rollout behind feature flag; enable on canary; monitor fallback rate and memory.
sara: I'll draft RFC with sequence diagrams, pseudocode for fast-path and fallback, perf numbers, and rollout plan.
ben: I'll add e2e test in prefix-e2e: concurrent append+demote+read across nodes with GC delay knob.
alex: I'll spike on metadata-path implementation. leo: I'll add the feature-flag and a smoke job. jing: I'll run perf runs at representative qps to tune CAS and TTL. maria: I'll triage canary results and watch telemetry.
sara: RFC draft by EOD tomorrow; will include rollback criteria (e.g., fallback rate >1% or memory growth).
maria: thanks all. this should close the flaky canary if metrics look good. :thumbsup:
